communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Custodian of Records, Harris County Sheriff's Office:

Under the Texas Public Information Act (Tex. Gov't Code ch. 552), I request the following existing
records, in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose (research and public education
regarding local detention practices).

I request the Sheriff's Office **arrest and booking log** (the jail booking records the Office maintains
in the ordinary course) for every individual booked into the Harris County Jail from **January 1, 2025
to the present**. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system records,
including:

1. Booking or system (SPN/SO) number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking/confinement;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field (including any
   notation your system enters for a hold or detainer);
6. Arresting/committing agency;
7. Warrant or reference number.

This is the Office's routine arrest/booking log — the same public jail-booking information reflected in
your public inmate/booking search — and I request it in the existing electronic format your
jail-management system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a
formatted report). If producing it requires programming or manipulation of data, § 552.231 requires a
written statement of whether it can be produced, in what form, and the cost and time — and then
production; every jail-management system can export its booking log.

I do not seek any confidential criminal-history record. The state identification (SID) number and any DPS
criminal-history record information may be withheld under § 411.083; I am not requesting it.

To be clear about scope: I am requesting the Office's general arrest/booking log for all bookings in this
period, which is public jail-booking information under the Act. I am not requesting records generated by
or for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement; any immigration-hold notation that appears in the
booking-charges field is incidental booking data the Office records for its own custody purposes, and does
not make the arrest/booking log confidential.

As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if fees will exceed
$40, please provide the itemized estimate required by § 552.2615 before incurring cost, and I will respond
promptly, including narrowing the date range (for example, quarter by quarter) if that helps. If the
Office intends to withhold any responsive information, it must timely request an Attorney General decision
under § 552.301; absent a timely request, the information is presumed public under § 552.302. Please also
preserve all responsive records pending resolution. Thank you.

Sincerely,
Glen Wasserstein
Immigration Law Group, P.C.
1717 K Street NW, Suite 900, Washington, DC 20006
glen@immigrationgroup.com | (929) 786-1863

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein
